question: If $\vec{a}=\hat{i}-2\hat{j}+\hat{k}$, $\vec{b}=2\hat{i}+\hat{j}-3\hat{k}$ and $\vec{a}+\vec{b}+\vec{c}=\vec{0}$, find $\vec{c}$.
explanation:
Step 1: From $\vec{a}+\vec{b}+\vec{c}=\vec{0}$, we obtain $\vec{c}=-(\vec{a}+\vec{b})$.
Step 2: Add the first two vectors: $\vec{a}+\vec{b}=(1+2)\hat{i}+(-2+1)\hat{j}+(1-3)\hat{k}$.
Step 3: Thus, $\vec{a}+\vec{b}=3\hat{i}-\hat{j}-2\hat{k}$.
Step 4: Taking its negative gives $\vec{c}=-3\hat{i}+\hat{j}+2\hat{k}$.
Step 5: This value makes the sum of all three vectors equal to $\vec{0}$.
Final Answer: $\vec{c}=-3\hat{i}+\hat{j}+2\hat{k}$.
